# Results — Study 709 (World-Series-Effect)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**the League (AL vs NL) of the World Series champion "predicts" next year's stock
market**, a baseball cousin of the Super Bowl Indicator, plus its city-mythology variant
(**a New York franchise winning "predicts" next year's market**). Offline & deterministic
once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of
**2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current year, 2026, is
dropped from the tape entirely — the still-open 2025 champion's "next year" call is
therefore not yet scoreable and sits outside every statistic below). Fingerprint
`50410c20273a` (^GSPC daily close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily ^GSPC close (19,284 rows), 1949-11-01 → 2026-06-30, resampled to December-close-to-December-close calendar-year returns (price-only — ^GSPC carries no dividends) |
| Champion table | **hardcoded** 76-season table of World Series champions, 1950 → 2025 (winner, league, host city, New-York flag); **75 seasons actually played** (1994 cancelled by the players' strike — a named quirk, not a silent gap). Source: MLB official postseason history / Baseball-Reference, cross-checked against Wikipedia's "List of World Series champions" |
| Events | **74** seasons pair a champion with a COMPLETE next-year return (1950 → 2024 champions scored against CY1951 → CY2025); the 2025 champion (Los Angeles Dodgers, NL) has no scoreable "next year" yet (CY2026 is open) |
| League split | AL champion 39 seasons · NL champion 35 seasons |
| City variant | New York franchise (Yankees / Giants / Mets / Brooklyn Dodgers) champion in **19** of 74 scoreable seasons |
| Statistics | Welch *t* for the bull/bear mean-return split (single, non-overlapping annual events — same design as sibling study 158); a **binomial test against the sample's own unconditional up-rate** (never a 50% coin — the base-rate trap that flatters every "predicts up" folk indicator); a Wilson interval on the hit rate; a 20,000-draw permutation test on the two-sided mean contrast; a separate two-sided binomial "myth-check" against a flat 50% coin |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention: a "next year" position is entered at the **December 31 close of the World Series season** and held through the following calendar year — the champion (and its league/city) is public information weeks before that entry, so this is a **zero-look-ahead scheduled entry**, the same convention as sibling study 637's FOMC calendar |
| Data quirks (named) | 1994 had no World Series (players' strike) — dropped, not imputed; the 2025 champion's next-year call is open and excluded, not force-scored; ^GSPC is price-only (no dividends) — labeled throughout |

No survivorship on the Signal axis: ^GSPC is an index, not a survivor panel, and every
World Series champion 1950-2025 that was actually played is included (no cherry-picking
of "clean" decades).

## The headline — NL win → bullish next year (the ported NFC mnemonic)

| quantity | NL-preceded years | AL-preceded years |
|---|--:|--:|
| n | 35 | 39 |
| mean next-year ^GSPC return | **+11.21%** | +7.16% |
| contrast | **+4.05 pp** | |
| Welch *t* | **+1.07** | |
| permutation *p* (20,000 draws, two-sided) | **0.2955** | |
| omen hit rate | **52.7%** (Wilson 95% [41.5%, 63.7%]) | |
| unconditional up-rate (the correct baseline) | 73.0% | |
| binomial *p* (hit-in-bull-years rate vs 73.0% baseline) | **0.3675** | |
| myth-check — beats a flat 50% coin? | *p* = 0.7275 (no) | |

The point estimate leans the claimed direction (+4 pp) but every inferential check fails
by a wide margin: Welch *t* = 1.07 is barely half the desk's bar of 2, the permutation
p-value says a random relabeling of "which seasons are NL" produces a contrast this large
**30% of the time**, and the omen's own hit rate (52.7%) sits *well below* the honest
baseline of 73.0% unconditional up-years — meaning "predicting bullish" after an NL
champion actually calls the market's direction *worse* than just assuming every year is
an up year, which it usually is anyway.

## The city variant — a New York franchise wins → bullish next year

| quantity | NY-preceded years | non-NY-preceded years |
|---|--:|--:|
| n | 19 | 55 |
| mean next-year ^GSPC return | +8.02% | **+9.43%** |
| contrast | **−1.41 pp** | |
| Welch *t* | **−0.33** | |
| permutation *p* (20,000 draws, two-sided) | **0.7512** | |
| omen hit rate | **39.2%** (Wilson 95% [28.9%, 50.6%]) | |
| unconditional up-rate (the correct baseline) | 73.0% | |
| binomial *p* (hit-in-bull-years rate vs 73.0% baseline) | **0.5896** | |
| myth-check — beats a flat 50% coin? | *p* = 0.0805 (no, and the wrong way) | |

The "Wall Street's hometown team" story doesn't even get the *sign* right in sample: the
point estimate runs **negative** (−1.41 pp), and the hit rate (39.2%) is not just
statistically indistinguishable from a coin — it is numerically *below* one, meaning a
New York title in this sample is a mild anti-signal, not a bullish omen. With *t* = −0.33
and permutation *p* = 0.75, none of this clears any bar; it is simply noise on 19
observations dressed up by 16 of the most economically dominant decades on the tape
happening to also be pinstriped ones.

## Could you trade it? — an omen-timing strategy vs buy-and-hold

Hold the S&P only in years flagged bullish by the omen; sit in cash (0%) otherwise, one
rebalance per season (transaction costs are immaterial to this conclusion).

| strategy | years held / total | annualized return | vs buy-and-hold |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Buy-and-hold (no timing) | 74 / 74 | **+7.75%/yr** | — |
| NL-omen timing | 35 / 74 | +4.68%/yr | **−3.06 pp/yr** |
| NY-omen timing | 19 / 74 | +1.73%/yr | **−6.01 pp/yr** |

Both omens *lose* to simply staying invested — sitting in cash roughly half (or
three-quarters) of the calendar throws away compounding that no folk indicator this weak
can pay back, before a single basis point of cost is even charged.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic annual-return generator with a random bull/bear flag (base rate matched to
the real NL share, 35/74 ≈ 47%) and a TUNABLE planted "omen" boost added to bull-flagged
years' next-year return; no network.

| world | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (boost = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.09** (sd 0.88), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted boost = +10.0 pp (seed 709) | **+3.01** |

The detector never fires on the null and lights up cleanly on a planted omen — the
real-tape null result above is the genuine article, not a blind spot in the harness.
*(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Neither variant clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar: NL-omen Welch
  *t* = **+1.07** (permutation *p* = 0.2955, binomial *p* = 0.3675 against the correct
  73.0% baseline); NY-omen Welch *t* = **−0.33** (permutation *p* = 0.7512), and its point
  estimate even runs the wrong direction. n = 74 (35/39 split) and 74 (19/55 split) are
  both too small to detect anything short of an implausibly large structural premium, and
  neither variant has ever had a proposed economic mechanism.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** An omen-timing strategy underperforms buy-and-hold by
  **3.06 pp/yr** (NL) or **6.01 pp/yr** (NY) — sitting out large stretches of a mostly-up
  market is expensive, and there is no signal underneath to pay for the missed
  compounding.
- **"Beats a coin?" — BUSTED.** NL-omen hit rate 52.7% (coin-test *p* = 0.7275) and
  NY-omen hit rate 39.2% (coin-test *p* = 0.0805, numerically *below* 50%) — neither
  variant reliably beats a flat coin flip, let alone the market's own 73.0% up-rate.
